title: Robotics Has Been Stuck for 70 Years — Deepak Pathak, Skild AI
talk_summary: Deepak Pathak argues robotics has stalled because it lacks a general brain and scalable data, and proposes an 'omni-body' model trained via a pre-train/post-train/deployment data flywheel across heterogeneous hardware. The transferable ideas are the data-flywheel pattern (cheap diverse pre-training data + small high-quality post-training data + deployment feedback) and end-to-end learning over hand-built pipelines.

takeaways.what_they_do: Split learning into pre-training on cheap, scalable, diverse but low-quality data, post-training on small high-quality data, and a deployment flywheel that feeds production data back into pre-training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to pre-train using data which is highly scalable and diverse but maybe low quality ... for post training you use data from telly operation
takeaways.numbers: less than 10 hours of data for robust omelette task; <1 hour robot data for human-video transfer

takeaways.technique: Small high-quality data beats large low-quality for the critical stage
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a tiny amount of high-fidelity, on-target data (teleop) for the final post-training stage instead of scaling cheap but off-target data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for post training you use data from telly operation ... very high quality but low in amount

takeaways.technique: One general model across heterogeneous tasks/hardware
takeaways.what_they_do: Train a single 'omni-body' brain that works across many robot types and tasks, so data from any deployment improves the shared model.

takeaways.technique: Deploy early to start the feedback loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Start real deployment now specifically so the data flywheel can begin, accepting that deployment is hard and messy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have to start deployment now so that we can have this data flywheel in a foreseeable future

takeaways.what_they_do: Replace planning/mapping/state-machine stacks with a single end-to-end model reading raw inputs and emitting actions, keeping only a thin low-level controller.
takeaways.evidence_quote: unlike traditional robotics pipelines where you have planning, mapping etc. This is an end toend brain
